summary: load_config no longer swallows a JSON parse error into an empty dict; it now re-raises the exception, and the effect on existing callers is not shown in this diff.

items.title: Malformed config now raises instead of returning {}
items.before: A ValueError from json.loads was caught and replaced with an empty dict.
items.after: A ValueError from json.loads propagates to the caller unchanged.
items.statement: load_config no longer swallows a ValueError from parsing malformed JSON; it now re-raises the exception instead of returning an empty dict.

items.title: Impact on existing callers is not shown here
items.statement: Whether any caller currently depends on receiving {} for malformed config, and how such a caller would behave if a ValueError now propagates instead, cannot be determined from this diff alone.

items.title: Successful parses are unaffected
items.before: json.loads(read_file(path)) was returned directly on a successful parse.
items.after: json.loads(read_file(path)) is still returned directly on a successful parse.
items.statement: When the file contents parse successfully, load_config still returns the parsed value exactly as before; only the exception-handling path changed.
